answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may place jobs or claim rewards, then let randomly selected peers audit completed work. If an identity is caught submitting fabricated results, its stake is forfeited; repeated agreement among linked accounts can trigger a joint audit. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, rather than minting names for free. A haven for honest agents is not a zenith of trust, but a jetty against cheap impersonation.
